questions.question_text: A rectangle has an area of $35$ m$^{2}$ and its length is $2$ m longer than its width. Find the width of the rectangle.

options.why: Reported the length $x+2$ instead of the width $x$ that the question asked for.
Did not reject the negative solution $x=-7$; a width must be positive.
Treated the area as a side length rather than forming $x(x+2)=35$.

questions.solution_text:
Let $x$ be the width, in metres.
$x(x+2)=35$
$x^{2}+2x=35$
$x^{2}+2x-35=0$
$(x+7)(x-5)=0$
$x=-7$ or $x=5$
A width cannot be negative, so $x=5$.
The width is $5$ m.

questions.question_text: A triangle has an area of $20$ cm$^{2}$ and its base is $3$ cm longer than its perpendicular height. Find the height of the triangle.

options.why: Reported the base $h+3$ instead of the height $h$ that the question asked for.
Did not reject the negative solution $h=-8$; a height must be positive.

questions.solution_text:
Let $h$ be the height, in centimetres.
$\frac{1}{2}\times(h+3)\times h=20$
$h(h+3)=40$
$h^{2}+3h=40$
$h^{2}+3h-40=0$
$(h+8)(h-5)=0$
$h=-8$ or $h=5$
A height cannot be negative, so $h=5$.
The height is $5$ cm.

questions.question_text: The product of two consecutive positive integers is $90$. Find the two integers.

options.why: These consecutive integers also multiply to $90$, but the question specifies positive integers.
Guessed neighbouring integers whose product is $72$, not $90$.
Used consecutive odd integers ($x$ and $x+2$) instead of consecutive integers ($x$ and $x+1$).

questions.solution_text:
Let $x$ be the smaller integer.
$x(x+1)=90$
$x^{2}+x=90$
$x^{2}+x-90=0$
$(x+10)(x-9)=0$
$x=-10$ or $x=9$
The integers are positive, so $x=9$.
The two integers are $9$ and $10$.

questions.question_text: Two positive numbers differ by $2$ and the sum of their squares is $130$. Find the two numbers.

options.why: These numbers differ by $2$ with squares summing to $130$, but the question specifies positive numbers.
Modelled the larger number as $x-2$ instead of $x+2$, subtracting the difference.
Added the difference to the wrong number, giving $x+2$ and $x+4$.

questions.solution_text:
Let $x$ be the smaller number, so the larger is $x+2$.
$x^{2}+(x+2)^{2}=130$
$x^{2}+x^{2}+4x+4=130$
$2x^{2}+4x-126=0$
$x^{2}+2x-63=0$
$(x+9)(x-7)=0$
$x=-9$ or $x=7$
The numbers are positive, so $x=7$.
The two numbers are $7$ and $9$.

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown upwards so that its height $h$ metres after $t$ seconds is $h=t(8-t)$. Find the times when the ball is at a height of $12$ m.

options.why: Solved for one root and stopped, missing that the ball reaches $12$ m twice.
Found the time of maximum height, $t=4$, rather than the times at height $12$.
Made a sign error in factorising $t^{2}-8t+12=0$, giving both roots negative.

questions.solution_text:
$t(8-t)=12$
$8t-t^{2}=12$
$t^{2}-8t+12=0$
$(t-2)(t-6)=0$
$t=2$ or $t=6$
The ball reaches $12$ m at $t=2$ s on the way up and again at $t=6$ s on the way down.

questions.question_text: The square of a positive number is $42$ more than the number itself. Find the number.

options.why: Did not reject the negative solution $x=-6$; the number must be positive.
Made a sign error in factorising $x^{2}-x-42=0$, reading the root as $+6$.
Took the constant in the problem as the answer rather than solving the equation.

questions.solution_text:
Let $x$ be the number.
$x^{2}=x+42$
$x^{2}-x-42=0$
$(x-7)(x+6)=0$
$x=7$ or $x=-6$
The number is positive, so $x=7$.
The number is $7$.

questions.question_text: A rectangular swimming pool measuring $12$ m by $8$ m is surrounded by a path of uniform width $x$ m. The area of the path alone is $224$ m$^{2}$. Find the width of the path.

options.why: Did not reject the negative solution $x=-14$; a width must be positive.
Set the outer area equal to $224$ instead of subtracting the pool area to isolate the path.
Halved the correct width, treating $2x$ as if it were the total added width $x$.

questions.solution_text:
The outer rectangle measures $(12+2x)$ by $(8+2x)$, and the path is the outer area minus the pool.
$(12+2x)(8+2x)-12\times8=224$
$96+24x+16x+4x^{2}-96=224$
$4x^{2}+40x-224=0$
$x^{2}+10x-56=0$
$(x+14)(x-4)=0$
$x=-14$ or $x=4$
A width cannot be negative, so $x=4$.
The path is $4$ m wide.

questions.question_text: A rectangle has a perimeter of $100$ m and an area of $225$ m$^{2}$. Find its dimensions.

options.why: Chose a pair summing to $50$ but $10\times40=400\neq225$.
Chose a pair summing to $50$ but $15\times35=525\neq225$.
Assumed a square of half-perimeter side, giving area $625$, not $225$.

questions.solution_text:
Let $x$ be the width, in metres. Half the perimeter is $50$, so the length is $50-x$.
$x(50-x)=225$
$50x-x^{2}=225$
$x^{2}-50x+225=0$
$(x-5)(x-45)=0$
$x=5$ or $x=45$
Both values are valid; they are the two dimensions of the same rectangle.
The rectangle is $5$ m by $45$ m.

questions.question_text: The product of two consecutive positive even integers is $224$. Find the two integers.

options.why: These consecutive even integers also multiply to $224$, but the question specifies positive integers.
Used consecutive integers ($x$ and $x+1$) instead of consecutive even integers ($x$ and $x+2$).
Started from the larger integer, giving $x+2$ and $x+4$.

questions.solution_text:
Let $x$ be the smaller even integer, so the next is $x+2$.
$x(x+2)=224$
$x^{2}+2x=224$
$x^{2}+2x-224=0$
$(x+16)(x-14)=0$
$x=-16$ or $x=14$
The integers are positive, so $x=14$.
The two integers are $14$ and $16$.
